ficha.descripcion: The Mercedes-Benz G-Class, colloquially known as the G-Wagen, is a series of four-wheel drive SUVs manufactured by Magna Steyr for Mercedes-Benz since 1979. It is characterized by its boxy styling and body-on-frame construction, and has since morphed into a luxury SUV line. Some versions feature a removable plastic hardtop.

ficha.descripcion: The Mercedes-Benz C-Klasse V6 DTM was a car raced by Mercedes-Benz in the Deutsche Tourenwagen Meisterschaft series (DTM) starting 1994 before it was replaced by the CLK-DTM in 2000. The first livery of the casting replicates the car driven by Klaus Ludwig in the 1994 Deutsche Tourenwagen Meisterschaft season for the AMG Mercedes D2 Privat Team. Ludwig won the 1994 championship. The tampo design for the first release is notably incredibly complex for a Hot Wheels car. The second livery of the car replicates Alexander Grau's Zakspeed Mercedes car for the 1995 DTM season. The base of the casting reads Mercedes-Benz AMG C-Class Racer.

ficha.descripcion: The NISMO 270R is a special production version of the Nissan Silvia K's, produced in 1994 to celebrate the 10th anniversary of NISMO, Nissan's tuning arm. The car was powered by a tuned 2.0L SR20DET turbocharged inline-4 producing 270 horsepower, mated to a 5-speed manual. 30 were produced, although NISMO also produced body kits to allow Silvia owners to replicate the appearance of the 270R. The base of the casting reads Nissan Silvia (S14) NISMO Customized.

ficha.descripcion: The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution III is the third generation of the Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution, the sports sedan and rally-tuned version of the Mitsubishi Lancer. The Evo III, as it is colloquially known, was designed by Akinori Nakanishi, Masaru Furukawa and Yasukichi Akamatsu and produced from 1995 to 1996. It featured more aggressive styling, added aerodynamic elements and other changes to improve airflow to the engine and brakes. The car's 2.0L 4G63T turbocharged inline-4 was fitted with a larger turbocharger, allowing the engine to produce 266 horsepower. 10,080 were produced.

ficha.descripcion: The Toyota MR2 is a two-seat sports car manufactured by Toyota. The second generation, designed by Kunihiro Uchida and internally named the W20, was introduced in 1989 following a radical redesign from the preceding generation, featuring a more rounded appearance; it is sometimes called a "poor man's Ferrari" due to a similar appearance to Ferrari's contemporary models such as the 308. Production ended in 1999. The TRD2000GT is a racing bodykit conversion for the Toyota MR2 designed by Toyota Racing Development. Customers had the ability to select engine, suspension, wheel and interior upgrades to their MR2 after the kit was selected; it is said that because of this no TRD2000GTs were alike. A total of 35 were produced. The base of the casting reads Toyota MR2 TRD 2000GT.

ficha.descripcion: The Porsche 911 GT1 Straßenversion is a limited-production homologation high-performance sports car manufactured by Porsche from 1996 to 1999. Designed by Herbert Ampferer, Norbert Singer, Horst Reitter, Harm Lagaay and Tony Hatter, the 911 GT1 Straßenversion was designed to homologate the 911 GT1 for GT1 competition, with regulations stipulating 25 cars be built for competition. The car is powered by a 3.2L M96/80 twin-turbocharged flat-6 mated to a 6-speed manual, detuned due to emissions regulations; the engine produced 536 horsepower and did 0-100 km/h (62 mph) in 3.8 seconds. 25 were produced. The base of the casting reads 97 Porsche 911 GT1.

ficha.descripcion: The Pagani Zonda is a mid-engined high-performance sports car manufactured by Pagani from 1999 to 2019. Designed by Horacio Pagani, the Zonda acted as Pagani's first product. The Zonda C12 S was the second version of the Zonda, unveiled at the 2002 Geneva Motor Show; it was powered by a 7.0L Mercedes-Benz M120 V12 making 542 horsepower, mated to a 6-speed manual; it acted as the replacement to the C12, originally introduced in 1999. Of note is that the C12 was still available when the C12 S was unveiled, being concurrently produced for about a year. The C12 S was produced from 2002 to 2005. 15 were produced. Pagani still manufactures versions on the Zonda, albeit only on request and typically in one-off versions. The base of the casting reads Pagani Zonda C12 S.

ficha.descripcion: The BMW M5 is the high-performance version of the BMW 5 Series, produced since 1984. The E39 5 Series, designed by Joji Nagashima, served as the platform for the third generation of the M5, powered by a 4.9L S62 V8. The E39 was the first M5 to use a V8 engine and the first to use aluminum front suspension components and multi-link rear suspension. A total of 20,482 cars were produced from 1999 to 2003. The base of the casting reads 2001 BMW M5 E39.

ficha.descripcion: The Honda NSX was a mid-engined two-seat sports car manufactured by Honda from 1990 to 2005. Styled by Ken Okuyama, Masahito Nakano, Shigeru Uehara and James Stevens, the NSX was Honda's flagship offering, intended to compete with such cars like the Ferrari 348. It was powered by a 3.0L C30B V6; this was changed to a 3.2L C32B V6 later in the car's life. The car was facelifted in 2002 to keep it modern-looking, with fixed xenon high-intensity discharge beams as opposed to pop-up headlights. The NSX-R was a performance-oriented version of the NSX, intended for customers who wanted a "no-compromise" experience on the track with their cars. The NSX was discontinued in 2005; the name would be revived in 2017 after some years of development.

ficha.descripcion: The Porsche Cayenne (pronounced "kay-enn") is a luxury crossover SUV manufactured by Porsche since 2002. The first generation, internally designated the 9PA and styled by Steve Murkett, was Porsche's first entry into the SUV market; the Cayenne was Porsche's first off-road capable vehicle since the Junior and Super Junior tractors in the 1950s, the first Porsche with four doors and the first Porsche built with a V8 engine since the 928. The car's name was coined by German advertising agent Manfred Gotta and was launched to an initially mixed reception which warmed over time due to its good performance, handling and powerful engines; the first generation was discontinued in 2010. The Cayenne has since become one of Porsche's sales leaders. This casting features a hitch to attach a trailer.

ficha.descripcion: The Jeep Grand Cherokee is a series of mid-size SUVs produced by FCA US LLC for their Jeep division. The SRT Trackhawk trim level, which this casting replicates, is the highest-performance trim level of the WK2 Grand Cherokee lineup, featuring most amenities from the less-powerful SRT 392 but with a 6.2L Hemi Hellcat V8 swapped in. The Grand Cherokee SRT Trackhawk is the most powerful car in the Jeep lineup. The casting was originally intended to have been released as a Hot Wheels id casting. A basketball is situated in the rear seats.

ficha.descripcion: The Porsche 911 GT3 is a high-performance homologation model of the Porsche 911, sitting above the 911 Turbo but below the GT2, initially introduced in 1999 with the 996 generation. The fourth generation of the GT3, based on the 992 generation of the Porsche 911, was unveiled in February 2021. Transmission options include a 7-speed dual clutch or a 6-speed manual. A Touring version featuring a retractable wing is also available. In August 2022 the 911 GT3 RS, a higher-performance version of the GT3, was introduced; it features a dramatically improved aerodynamic profile and a wing incorporating active aerodynamics, along with an uprated 4.0L MA2.75 flat-6 now making 517 BHP.

ficha.descripcion: The Nissan Z GT4 is a grand touring racing sports car manufactured by Nissan for Group GT4 competition. It is essentially a racing version of the 2023 Nissan Z, featuring the same 3.0L VR30DDTT twin-turbocharged V6 as the road-going car but now outputting 450 horsepower. The car was previewed in 2022 by a "Racing Concept" version of the Z used in the 2022 Super Taikyu Series. The car currently competes in the Super Taikyu Series, Michelin Pilot Challenge and the GT4 America Series among other series. Deliveries of cars begun in 2023.

ficha.descripcion: The Toyota GR Corolla is a high-performance version of the Toyota Corolla hatchback produced starting 2022 as a 2023 model year model. Designed by Sung-won Lee and Masayuki Sugiura and internally designated the GZEA14, the GR Corolla was designed mainly for the United States market as a "complement" to the GR Yaris, which is not sold in the United States. The GR Corolla is powered by a 1.6L G16E-GTS turbocharged inline-3, mated to a 6-speed manual. There also exist the Circuit Edition and Morizo Editions of the GR Corolla, featuring enhancements over the standard GR Corolla. The first release features a livery replicating that of Ryan Tuerck's Papadakis Racing Toyota GR Corolla drift car. The base of the casting reads 23 Toyota Corolla GR.

ficha.descripcion: The GMC Sierra is a range of trucks manufactured by General Motors under their GMC brand; it is effectively GMC's counterpart to the Chevrolet Silverado. The fourth generation, styled by Tyler Moffett, debuted in March 2018 and differentiates itself from the Silverado with a two-piece tailgate, carbon fiber pickup bed, rearview mirror backup camera system, heads-up display and distinct styling. The Sierra was restyled in 2022 by Thomas Bergeron, while two additional trim levels were introduced, namely the AT4X and Denali Ultimate. This generation is expected to be replaced in 2026 with a new generation of Sierra. This casting features a hitch to attach a trailer.

ficha.descripcion: The BMW M5 is the high-performance version of the BMW 5 Series, produced since 1984. The seventh generation of the M5, styled by José Casas and internally designated the G90, was based on the G60 generation of the 5 Series and entered production in 2024 for the 2025 model year. Introduced in June 2024, the G90 M5 is BMW's first plug-in hybrid M5 model; it is powered by a 4.4L S68 twin-turbocharged V8 paired with an electric motor system to produce a combined 717 horsepower. A station wagon version, the M5 Touring, was also made available in this generation; it was the first M5 to be made available in this configuration since 2010.

ficha.descripcion: The Mercedes-AMG GT is a two-door sports car marketed by Mercedes-AMG. The second generation, introduced at the 2023 Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance, was styled by Slavche Tanevski and succeeds the previous generation AMG GT. In comparison to the previous AMG GT the current generation AMG GT is longer and seats four as opposed to two. The AMG GT 63 PRO is a high-performance version of the AMG GT, powered by a 4.0L M177 twin-turbocharged V8 mated to an 9-speed Speedshift MCT 9G-Tronic automatic; the car produces 603 horsepower and is all-wheel drive.

ficha.descripcion: The De Tomaso Pantera was a mid-engined sports car produced by De Tomaso Automobili from 1971 to 1992. Designed by Tom Tjaarda of Ghia, the Pantera was the successor of the Mangusta and debuted at Modena in 1970. As was tradition with many De Tomaso cars, the Pantera used an American V8, which in this case was a 5.8L Ford Cleveland V8. 7,260 were produced. This casting is a depiction of a Pantera GTS prepared for Group 4 racing. The "351" number on the side is a reference to the capacity of the engine in cubic inches (351 ci/5.8L). The initial livery of this casting is based on the Panteras run by the De Tomaso works team in Group 4 competition.

ficha.descripcion: The Datsun 720 is a pickup truck manufactured by Nissan under their Datsun brand from 1979 to 1991. The successor to the 620, the 720 featured a more squared off design compared to its predecessors and was available in a number of different formats. It was named a number of different names in other countries. This casting is based on a Datsun 720 King Cab pickup modified for off-road racing; a pair of gloves and other things can be found behind the seats. The rear bracing will always feature a ORRR8DOT spare tire no matter what the main tire type is. This casting was named the Datsun Off-Road Racer in development.

ficha.descripcion: The Jaguar E-Type, known as the XK-E in the American market, is a front-mid-engined sports car manufactured by Jaguar from 1961 to 1974. Designed by Malcolm Sayer, the E-Type was based on the racing D-Type and employed a front subframe carrying the engine, front suspension and front bodywork bolted directly to the bodytub. The cars were powered by a 3.8L XK inline-6. The car has consistently been cited as one of the most pleasant-looking cars ever made. The Lightweight E-Type, essentially a racing version of the E-Type, was introduced in 1963 as a follow-up to the D-Type. These made use of extensive amounts of aluminum and were fitted with a tuned version of the 3.8L XK inline-6, fitted with an aluminum engine block, mated to either a 4- or 5-speed ZF manual; this engine produced about 300

ficha.descripcion: "Jay Leno Tank Car" is a common name used to refer to the Blastolene Special, a custom hot rod built for American comedian and television host Jay Leno by American craftsman Randy Grubb. Built in Grubb's workshop in Grants Pass, Oregon, the Blastolene Special is powered by a 29.4L Continental AV1790-5B V12 from an M47 Patton with a Greyhound transmission; Leno has since made modifications to the car, fitting the engine with twin Banks Engineering turbochargers and fuel injection and changing the gearbox to a 6-speed Allison unit. As a result, the car is estimated to produce 1,600 BHP.

Designed by Christian von Koenigsegg, the Agera features a 5.0L twin-turbocharged V8 producing 960 horsepower. The Agera R is a version of the Agera produced from 2011 to 2014 with improved performance and higher power output, notable for setting a number of speed records. 18 were produced. The car is notable for its appearance in the film Need For Speed; however the car featured in the film was a replica constructed by Race Car Replicas powered by a Chevrolet LS engine. ficha.descripcion: Kousoku Hauler (pronounced "koh-so-koo") is a 1990s-style Japanese truck modified as a twin-car carrier. The word kōsoku (Kanji: 高速) literally translates to "high speed". Essentially a Japanese analog to the Second Story Lorry, Kousoku Hauler features an angled second deck which can be used to transport a second car. A tow rope can be seen in the bottom deck. This casting was named the Japan Double Decker Hauler in development.

ficha.descripcion: The Lamborghini Essenza SCV12 is a track-only high-performance sports car produced by Lamborghini under their Squadra Corse motorsports division. Designed by Mitja Borkert and developed according to FIA prototype safety rules, the car uses the same 6.5L L539 V12 as the Aventador SVJ but features numerous modifications to allow the car to become the most powerful V12-powered car in Lamborghini's lineup. Production totaled 40 cars, with each costing $2.5 million. Deliveries began in December 2020. ficha.descripcion: The Lancia Delta S4 is a rally car manufactured by Abarth for Lancia intended for competition in the FIA World Rally Championship. Designed by Renato Sconfienza, Bruno Giardino and Sergio Limone under Pier Paolo Messori, the Delta S4 was homologated for Group B and acted as the successor to the 037. It was powered by a 1.8L Tipo 233 ATR 18S twincharged inline-4 mated to a 5-speed Hewland transmission; the engine produced 550 horsepower. ficha.descripcion: The MG Metro 6R4 (6-Cylinder, Rally, 4-Wheel Drive) is a racing version of the Austin Metro, prepared for Group B racing. Powered by a Rover V64V 3.0L V6, the Metro 6R4 effectively only shared a superficial resemblance with its the car it took its name from as the racing version was a mid-engined all-wheel drive vehicle. The car was moderately successful in competition but due to the banning of Group B on the grounds of safety the car had a short-lived career in its intended series; it then moved to other racing series. About 205 road-going versions were built for homologation purposes. The initial livery is a replica of Didier Auriol and Bernard Ocelli's car with a different number. In development this casting was named the '86 MG Metro 6R4.

ficha.descripcion: The Mazda RX-3 is a rotary-engined automobile sold by Mazda from 1971 to 1978, it essentially being a rotary-engined version of the Grand Familia, which was largely identical in appearance. The RX-3 was available in sedan, coupe and wagon styles, with the wagon being known as the RX-3 Sports Wagon. The RX-3 Sports Wagon was the world's first rotary-engined wagon and was sold from 1972 to 1976; production of all RX-3s ended in 1978 to make way for the RX-7. The RX-3 was the most successful and popular of all of Mazda's pre-RX-7 rotary models.

ficha.descripcion: The Porsche 911 GT3 R is a grand touring racing sports car manufactured by Porsche for use in Group GT3 competition. Originally introduced in 1999, the GT3 R is currently in its fourth generation, based on the Porsche 992 platform. It is powered by a 4.2L M97/80 flat-6, now making 565 horsepower. The car competes in racing series such as the World Endurance Championship, IMSA SportsCar Championship and various branches of the GT World Challenge; it made its racing debut at the 2023 24 Hours of Daytona. The initial livery of the casting is based on Rexy, the affectionate nickname for the 911 GT3 R raced by AO Racing in the IMSA SportsCar Championship with a T. rex-inspired livery; the chase livery is based on Roxy, a pink "female" version of Rexy.

ficha.descripcion: The Porsche 917K is a sports prototype racing car manufactured by Porsche for use in endurance racing. Designed by Helmuth Bott, the 917K was a short-tailed version of the 917 family, competing from 1970 to 1971 with some revisions in the design. The 1970 917K was powered by a 4.5L Typ 912 flat-12 producing 580 horsepower, mated to a 5-speed manual. A highly successful race car, the 917 won numerous major endurance races and was one of the first in a line of highly successful Porsche sports prototype race cars which would continue to dominate endurance racing in the following decades. The initial livery of this casting replicates chassis 917-004/017 as driven by Brian Redman and Jo Siffert in the 1970 24 Hours of Le Mans. The base of the casting reads Porsche 917 K.

ficha.descripcion: The Porsche 917KH debuted in the collector-aimed 100% line in the Porsche 50th Anniversary 4-Car Set. It featured an opening rear hatch which displayed a detailed engine. In 2005, it was re-tooled without the opening rear hatch. It was one of the two 100% Hot Wheels castings to stay in production after the series ended, the other being the Toyota Off-Road Truck. Most liveries used by this casting depict 917KHs that have raced (e.g. the 1998 100% Hot Wheels and 2013 Gulf Racing versions are based on 917-022 as used in the film Le Mans, the 2001 100% Hot Wheels and 2025 Car Culture releases are based on 1970 24 Hours of Le Mans winner 917-023 etc.).

ficha.descripcion: The Sakura Sprinter is a Hot Wheels casting which debuted in the 2018 Car Culture: Team Transport Series. It is a Hot Wheels original design based on a 'Japanese-Style Box Truck' and bears resemblance to the Hino ZM Series COE of the 1960's and 70's. It has an opening rear door which serves as a ramp to drive a car into the plastic cargo box. The Sakura Sprinter shares a nearly identical but slightly smaller cab design with Stuntin' Semi.

ficha.descripcion: The Subaru Legacy is a mid-sized car manufactured by Subaru from 1989 to 2025. The fourth generation Legacy, produced from 2003 to 2009 and codenamed BL and BP, was designed by Tōru Ōzeki, Hiroyuki Kobayashi and Tetsuya Jirōbō; it featured a complete redesign from the previous generation and was launched on 23 May 2003 in Japan. The Legacy GT was a more performance-oriented version of the Legacy, featuring all-wheel drive and either a 5-speed automatic or 6-speed manual. This casting is based on a 2005 Subaru Legacy GT owned by Hot Wheels Development Program Management Associate Antonio Gaido. In the trunk is a remote-controlled Subaru Impreza 22B STi, referencing a RC car owned by Gaido himself.

ficha.descripcion: The Toyota 4Runner (read: "forerunner") is a mid-sized sport utility vehicle (originally compact) sold around the world since 1984, replacing in North America the older Toyota Trekker, which was essentially a Toyota Hilux converted into an SUV by Winnebago. The sixth generation 4Runner, styled by Adam Rabinowitz and Kevin Hunter and introduced in 2024 for the 2025 model year, is built on the same platform as the Tacoma and shares many mechanical components with it; the 4Runner TRD Pro is a high-performance off-road trim, being powered by a 2.4L T24A-FTS turbocharged inline-4 with an iForce MAX hybrid system. Despite only being available in left-hand drive form the 4Runner is still built at Toyota's Tahara Plant in Aichi.

ficha.descripcion: The Toyota FJ Cruiser is a retro-styled SUV marketed by Toyota from 2006 to 2022. Styled by Jin-won Kim and initially shown off as a concept car in 2003, the car was ultimately greenlit for production following positive consumer response. It features styling inspired by that of the J40-series Land Cruiser. The car shares many structural underpinnings with the Land Cruiser Prado and is manufactured by Hino Motors on Toyota's behalf.

ficha.descripcion: The Volkswagen Corrado is a compact four-seat liftback coupe produced by Karmann in Germany for Volkswagen from 1988 to 1995. Designed by Herbert Schäfer, the car essentially acted as the replacement for the Scirocco. The VR6 was a more performance-oriented version of the Corrado, featuring a VR6 engine, wider front track and slightly updated styling. Production ended in 1995, to be replaced by the Scirocco. 97,521 were produced. This casting depicts a modified Corrado with a bodykit.

The car was noted for its ponton styling, and was also notable for being the first car to provide front seatbelts as standard, in addition to providing three-point seatbelts as standard. The car was initially introduced as the Amason, but German motorcycle manufacturer Kreidler had registered the name; both companies agreed that the Amason name could only be used within Sweden, and the spelling was changed to Amazon some time after. The wagon was produced from 1962 to 1969. 667,791 Amazons of all body styles were produced. ficha.descripcion: The Lykan HyperSport is a highly-exclusive supercar designed and manufactured by Lebanese-founded Emirati automotive company W Motors. Designed by Ralph Debbas, Anthony Janarelly and Benoit Fraylon, the HyperSport was the first supercar to be designed and manufactured exclusively in the Middle East. Priced at $3.4 million, the HyperSport was the third most expensive car at the time of its production; it features a Ruf-sourced 3.7L flat-6 producing 760 BHP and also features diamond-encrusted headlights. Only seven cars were produced, including one for the Dubai Police. The car was prominently featured in the movie Furious 7; ten replicas using the same molds as the production cars were produced for the film. At the end of filming, one car was given to W Motors and displayed in their showroo

ficha.descripcion: Designed by in-house Ford-fanatic Abe Lugo. The Lincoln Futura was a concept car created in 1955. Ahead of it's time, a futuristic look was created with the bubble top along with some radical fenders in the back as well as some specail treatment for the headlights and front grille. The concept car was presented in a Pearl White, just like the premiere issue of the Hot Wheels version. It was one of the first real world cars to sport a pearl paint. About a decade later, George Barris would get hold of the car, and turn it into one of the most recognizable and recreated cars to date, the Batmobile.

ficha.descripcion: The 51 Le Sabre Concept is based upon the real Le Sabre concept car, designed by Harley J. Earl and built by GM in 1951. It was featured in car shows around the world and sports the "jet airplane" look that was so prevalent in the 1950's. The car was powered by a 215 c.i. V-8 engine (≈ 3.5 L) with a Buick Dynaflow automatic transmission. The original car employed two carburetors - one which ran on premium gasoline when driving normally and another which used methanol when the accelerator pedal was stomped. This Hot Wheels faithfully recreates the silvery finish of the original, which the designer himself used as a daily driver. Still being shown in a General Motors museum, after 60 years, it still catches the eye.

ficha.descripcion: The Chrysler Turbine Car is an experimental two-door turbine-powered coupe produced by the Chrysler Corporation from 1963 to 1964. Styled by Chrysler design chief Elwood Engel, the car was powered by an Chrysler A831 turbine engine, mated to a 3-speed TorqueFlite automatic. Assembly of the car was mostly done in Turin, Italy by Carrozzeria Ghia; final assembly was completed in Detroit by Chrysler. ficha.descripcion: This casting was based on (and inspired by) the Monroe Handler Mustang II of 1977. Built by Monroe Shocks and Hot Rod magazine, the original Monroe Handler was built to showcase Monroe’s new Handler line of shocks. The building of the Monroe Handler was chronicled in Hot Rod Magazine June, July and August issues. A one-off production based on the Mustang II, the Monroe Handler had a number of significant improvements, including a Roush-tuned 363ci engine producing 400 horses and a modified suspension. The car also featured an upgraded exterior with steel IMSA-style fenders and other enhancements by Creative Car Craft.

ficha.descripcion: The Plymouth Savoy is a series of full- or mid-sized automobiles produced by the Plymouth division of the Chrysler Corporation from 1954 to 1964. The Savoy name had been used on a number of other vehicles prior, such as a station wagon. When introduced the car was positioned between the Plaza and the Belvedere; power steering was added in 1955 and a hardtop coupe and station wagon in 1956. Production of the Savoy ended in 1964 where it was replaced by the Fury I. This casting depicts the 1955 Plymouth Savoy modified by Alex Taylor and Lucky Costa of HOT ROD Garage.

ficha.descripcion: The Chevrolet C/K is a series of trucks manufactured by the Chevrolet division of General Motors. The third generation of the C/K, styled by Bill Mitchell, was introduced in 1973 and was known as the Rounded Line series. This generation of C/K introduced a four door cab configuration as well as trim levels, including the Cheyenne, Scottsdale and Silverado trims. The vehicle's styling included a recessed front grille with orange turn signals; 1974 added an option for door-mounted drip moldings, with those becoming standard in 1975. The third generation C/K was discontinued in 1991, although it was superseded midway through 1988 with a new generation of C/K truck.

ficha.descripcion: The Volkswagen Type 2 is a series of commercial vehicles manufactured by Volkswagen; the first generation, designated the T1 and designed by Ben Pon, was introduced in 1949 and featured a split-screen front windshield. The Samba Bus, officially the Kleinbus Sonderausführung (lit. "small bus special version"), was a version of the T1 with twenty-one or twenty-three windows and a skylight roof. The origin of the Samba name is unclear although it first appeared in Dutch literature. T1 production ended in 1967. This casting depicts a 1967 Volkswagen Bus owned by American comedian Gabriel Iglesias, named "Iron Man"; Iglesias is notable for owning numerous Volkswagen buses.

ficha.descripcion: The Toyota 4Runner (read: "forerunner") is a mid-sized sport utility vehicle (originally compact) sold around the world since 1984, replacing the older Toyota Trekker which was essentially a Toyota Hilux converted into an SUV by Winnebago. Despite being manufactured in Japan at Toyota's Tahara Plant the car is mainly manufactured for export; the car was however sold in Japan until 2009 with the name Hilux Surf. The second generation 4Runner, introduced in 1989, featured a freshly-designed body on Hilux underpinnings although both cars still shared many parts. Facelifts occurred in 1993 and 1995, with production ending the same year. The base of the casting reads 93 Toyota 4Runner.

ficha.descripcion: The Chevrolet Tahoe is a full-sized SUV marketed by the Chevrolet division of General Motors since 1995. The first generation, styled by Wayne Cherry, was introduced in 1995 as a badge-engineered version of the GMC Yukon, itself based on the C/K series of the time; it was intended as a replacement for the K5 Blazer and was offered in three and five-door formats. The Tahoe was offered in three trim levels; base, LS and LT, none of which were shared with the Blazer. Production ended in 1999. This casting is based on a lowered 1995 Chevrolet Tahoe. A powerful sound system can be found in the rear of the car. The base of the casting reads 1995 Chevy Tahoe.

ficha.descripcion: The Subaru Impreza WRX STI is a high-performance version of the Subaru Impreza. Designed by Hidefumi Kato, the second generation Impreza WRX was introduced in 2000, featuring a 2.0L EJ207 turbocharged flat-4 and a 5-speed TY75 manual; the WRX STI would use the same engine but feature a stronger 6-speed TY856 manual instead. Initially noted for its controversial styling, leading to its name of "bugeye", the WRX STI, as well as the Impreza line as a whole, was restyled in 2003 by Peter Stevens and again in 2005 by Andreas Zapatinas; these iterations were named the "blobeye" and "hawkeye" respectively. The "hawkeye" design was intended to resemble a jet intake and wings, paying tribute to Subaru's aircraft manufacturing roots, and was used from 2005 to 2007. This generation of Impreza WRX STI

The first generation, styled by John Doughty and Claude Lobo, was unveiled at the 1998 Geneva Motor Show; it took its name from an earlier concept car shown off by Ghia in 1991, Ford's European styling partner. It debuted a new design language, named New Edge, which was deemed as polarizing. The Focus RS was a high-performance version of the Focus, being introduced in 2002 and produced until 2003. It was powered by a 2.0L Duratec-RS turbocharged inline-4 mated to a 5-speed Ford MTX-75 manual and was built at Ford's Saarlouis Plant. 4,501 were produced.

ficha.descripcion: The Cadillac CTS is a luxury car marketed and manufactured by Cadillac from 2004 to 2019 across three generations. The second generation, styled by John Manoogian II, was unveiled at the 2007 North American International Auto Show. The CTS-V was a high-performance version of the CTS, using a 6.2L LSA supercharged V8, and was available in coupe, sedan and wagon formats, known as the Sport Wagon; the CTS-V Sport Wagon was unveiled at the 2010 New York International Auto Show. Production of the second generation CTS ended in 2014, and along with it the wagon.

ficha.descripcion: The Toyota Alphard is a large luxury-oriented minivan manufactured by Toyota since 2002. The third generation of the Alphard, introduced in 2015, was designed by Kenichi Yoshioka and featured a completely redesigned exterior and a number of new engine choices. The Alphard was developed similarly to "a luxury sedan with a large space" and emphasizes focus on ride comfort levels and styling. This generation of Alphard was discontinued in 2023 with the introduction of the next generation of Alphard. A booster seat can be found in the car, added in commemoration of the birth of designer Ronald Wong's nephew.

The base of the casting reads Honda S2000 20th Anniversary.

ficha.descripcion: The Lamborghini Revuelto is a high-performance hybrid sports car produced by Lamborghini. Designed by Mitja Borkert, the Revuelto acts as the successor to the Aventador. The Revuelto is powered by a 6.5L L545 V12 mated to an 8-speed Graziano dual clutch, assisted by three electric motors; the car produces 1,001 horsepower and is the first Lamborghini to adopt a plug-in hybrid drivetrain. The car incorporates Lamborghini's ALA system and an active rear wing as aerodynamic implements. Production began in 2023, priced at $608,358. The base of the casting reads Lamborghini Revuelto.

ficha.descripcion: The Amphicar Model 770 was a German amphibious two-seat automobile manufactured by the Quandt Group from 1960 to 1965 and marketed until 1968. Designed by Hans Trippel, the Amphicar was a spiritual successor to the Volkswagen Type 128 and 166 and the Trippel SG6 schwimmwagens. The car was powered by a 1.1L Triumph inline-4 and could drive on both land and water, offering modest performance in both aspects. 3,878 were produced. This casting depicts an Amphicar with a blown engine.

ficha.descripcion: The Honda Civic EG is a compact car produced by Honda as part of the fifth generation of Civic. Designed by Kohichi Hirata and replacing the fourth generation Civic, the fifth generation Civic was available in three body styles, each with a different internal code. Produced from 1991 to 1995, when it was replaced by the sixth generation Civic, the fifth generation has gained a cult following since, particularly the EG hatchback models. This casting is based on a modified 1992 Honda Civic EG with a VeilSide-style bodykit, representing Hector's Civic Hatchback, as seen briefly in The Fast and the Furious.

ficha.descripcion: The Golden Submarine was an early race car designed and built by Fred Offenhauser and Harry Miller for Barney Oldfield in 1917. It was designed to be fast and durable as well as being able to protect its driver in the event of an accident. Costing $15,000 to build, the Golden Submarine was powered by a 289 ci (4.7L) inline-4 producing 136 horsepower built by Miller. It was known to have competed in 54 races, winning 20 of them. The Golden Submarine was last owned by J. Allen Sloan of Illinois, where it is said to have been destroyed at an indeterminate time after being stored in one of Sloan's barns which caught fire. Many replicas are known to have been built.

ficha.descripcion: The Toyota GR Yaris is a sport compact car manufactured by Toyota since 2020. Designed by Shōta Itō, Takeo Okuno and Byung-kang Cho, the GR Yaris was designed essentially as a homologation special for World Rally Championship rules. The car itself is powered by a 1.6L G16E-GTS turbocharged inline-3 mated to a 6-speed Toyota EA67F manual (although an 8-speed GR-DAT automatic has been made available since 2024); the car produces up to 300 horsepower. The car itself is all-wheel drive and is only available for sale in markets where the standard Yaris is sold; it is built on a dedicated production line at Toyota's Motomachi Plant. Markets which did not receive the GR Yaris would receive the GR Corolla instead.

ficha.descripcion: The Vector W8 is a high-performance American sports car designed by Jerry Wiegert and David Kostka. The car was built using the latest aerospace materials, with Wiegert referring to the manufacture of the car as "aeromotive engineering"; the car was powered by a 6.0L Rodeck racing V8 with variable boost twin turbochargers. In essence, the W8 was a highly refined version of the W2 prototype, featuring a very similar appearance. Production was forced to halt when Vector was forcefully taken over by MegaTech, an Indonesian company with Bermudan ties; 22 were produced. According to designer Manson Cheung, there are no current plans to re-release this casting or other Vectors into the mainline or Premium lines due to licensing issues.

This casting depicts a heavily modified 2009 Ford Transit Connect with a widebody kit, mid-engine layout, a new hood with NACA ducts, rear ducktail-style wing, lowered ride height and dual exhausts poking out the tailgate. The interior can be seen by flipping a tab on the base to release the body from the base. The supercharged V8 engine is all-metal and the vehicle is right-hand-drive.

ficha.descripcion: The Chevrolet Advance Design is a series of trucks manufactured by Chevrolet from 1947 to 1955. It was their first major redesign of truck after World War II with a sleeker design compared to the previous AK series of trucks. It was available in a number of different formats, such as pickup truck, cab over engine, station wagon and even SUV in the form of the Chevrolet Suburban. A highly successful design, Chevrolet trucks were the best selling trucks in the United States in all the years it was sold. The Advance Design line was replaced with the Task Force line in 1956. This casting has no interior piece.

ficha.descripcion: The Porsche 906, also known as the Carrera 6, was a Group 4 sports car produced by Porsche AG in 1966. Designed by Erwin Komenda, the car was based on the 904 and lightened by using a fiberglass body instead of steel. Powered by a 2.0L Typ 771 flat-6, the car was first raced at the 1966 24 Hours of Daytona, driven by Hans Herrmann and Herbert Linge, where it won its class and would go on to be successful. The car was further developed into the 910, which raced from the middle of 1966. The initial livery of this casting is based on chassis 906-125, driven by Pauli Toivonen and Antti Aarnio-Wihuri for VW-Auto Oy in the 1966 World Sportscar Championship.

ficha.descripcion: The 92 Jeep Wrangler Sahara is a replica of the staff vehicles used at Jurassic Park in the eponymous film. The Jeeps used are based on the YJ generation of the Jeep Wrangler. Graphics for the model were done by Andrés Andrieu. Packaging design was done by Florence Jo, with graphics used to recreate various scenes from the movie. The bundle was available both on-site at Comic-Con and through Mattel Creations where it retailed for $30. The original casting features Dr. Ian Malcolm (Jeff Goldblum) waking up from a nap in the rear of the Jeep. The casting was retooled by Ronald Wong in 2025 for use in the standard Premium line to remove that feature.

ficha.descripcion: The 70 Chevy Blazer is a Hot Wheels casting designed by Brendon Vetuskey which debuted as part of the 2011 Hot Wheels Garage Series. It is based on the First Generation Chevrolet Blazer produced from 1969 to 1972, which was designed to compete with the Ford Bronco. It combined the off-road capabilities of its competitors, with the 'luxury' features found in pickup trucks at the time. Chevrolet sold over 70,000 First Generation Blazers during its four year production, before being updated for the 1973 model year.

ficha.descripcion: The Dodge Ram Van, alternatively the Dodge B-Series, is a series of full-sized vans and commercial vehicles produced by the Dodge division of the Chrysler Corporation. It was produced from 1971 to 2003 with relatively little changes in its platform, mainly at the Pillette Road Truck Assembly in Ontario, Canada. The Ram Van acted as a successor to the Dodge A100 and was restyled significantly in 1979 to make its appearance more in line with that of the Dodge Ram trucks of the time. When it was discontinued the Ram Van was replaced by the Dodge Sprinter. This casting is a recreation of the 1979 Dodge Ram Van as featured in the film Old School. This was Antonio Gaido's first Hot Wheels design.

ficha.descripcion: The BMW 7 Series is a series of luxury cars produced by BMW as the flagship car of their line. The first generation of the 7 Series, the E23, was styled by Paul Bracq and Manfred Rennen and introduced in 1977. It is notable for having introduced many features on a BMW, such as an on-board computer, service interval indicator, warning lights to indicate system faults to the driver, voice recorder and an advanced climate control system; it was also the first BMW to offer ABS, a driver's airbag and a new design of front suspension. The 733i was powered by a 3.2L M30B32 inline-6 produced from 1977 to 1984. The base of the casting reads 83 BMW 733i.

ficha.descripcion: The Chevrolet K5 Blazer is a full-sized sport utility vehicle built by General Motors from 1969 to 1994. Originally built on the K10 truck platform, the Blazer was positioned to compete against the International Harvester Scout and the Ford Bronco. Early models featured convertible tops until 1975, when they were replaced with a hardtop which was safer during rollovers. The vehicle was a sales success, quickly becoming popular and outsold its rivals. This is a replica of the Chevrolet K5 Blazer as driven by Hawkins Police Department Chief Jim Hopper (David Harbour) in Stranger Things; Hopper's hat can be seen in the front passenger seat. The base of the casting reads 1985 Chevy Blazer.

ficha.descripcion: The BMW M5 is the high-performance version of the BMW 5 Series, produced since 1984. The sixth generation of the M5, styled by Seungmo Lim and internally designated the F90, was based on the G30 generation of the 5 Series and entered production in 2017. Introduced at the 2017 Frankfurt Motor Show, the F90 M5 is the first M5 to feature an all-wheel drive system. It is powered by the same 4.4L S63 twin-turbocharged V8 as its predecessor, now producing 591 horsepower and mated to an 8-speed ZF GA8HP75Z automatic. Production ended in 2023 to be replaced by a new generation of M5.

The sixth generation of the M5, styled by Seungmo Lim and internally designated the F90, was based on the G30 generation of the 5 Series and entered production in 2017. Introduced at the 2017 Frankfurt Motor Show, the F90 M5 is the first M5 to feature an all-wheel drive system. It is powered by the same 4.4L S63 twin-turbocharged V8 as its predecessor, now producing 591 horsepower and mated to an 8-speed ZF GA8HP75Z automatic. Production ended in 2023 to be replaced by a new generation of M5.

ficha.descripcion: Airwolf is an advanced prototype supersonic attack helicopter designed by Charles Henry Moffet and built by "the Firm"; it is the focal point and the namesake of the Airwolf TV series. The helicopter is fitted with turbojet intakes, in-air refueling nozzle, machine guns and all-directional firing rocket launcher pods and is capable of flying up to Mach 2. It is typically flown by Stringfellow Hawke. The actual helicopter was modified from a Bell 222 (S/N 47085, tail number N3176S) owned by Van Nuys-based Jetcopters, Inc. The helicopter's modifications were designed by American artist Andrew Probert. The helicopter was flown in-series by Peter McKernan Sr., owner of Jetcopters. Following the cancelation of the show, the helicopter's modifications were removed and are now owned by a private

ficha.descripcion: The Aston Martin V8 is a grand touring sports car manufactured by Aston Martin from 1969 to 1989 over five series. Styled by William Towns, the V8 acted as the successor to the DB6, with Aston Martin had wanted to replace with a more modern looking model. As the name suggests the car is powered by a 5.3L V8. The car was marketed for a time as "Britan's Fastest Supercar" for its 170 mph (274 km/h) top speed. 4,021 were produced from 1969 to 1989. The V8 has also appeared in mass media, with the V8 appearing in the James Bond film The Living Daylights; the car used in the film was a Series 4 V8 Volante owned by Aston Martin chairman Victor Gauntlett with the license plate B549 WUU and was driven by Timothy Dalton, the actor for James Bond. Later in the movie the car is fitted with a hardtop

ficha.descripcion: The Aston Martin V12 Vanquish is a two-door grand touring sports car manufactured by Aston Martin from 2001 to 2007. Designed by Ian Callum, the V12 Vanquish acted as the successor to the Virage and was powered by a 5.9L AM03 V12 making 480 horsepower, mated to a 6-speed manual. The V12 Vanquish was refreshed into the V12 Vanquish S in 2004 while the V12 Vanquish was discontinued in 2005. 1,492 were produced; the V12 Vanquish would be replaced by the DBS V12 in 2007. The V12 Vanquish is also notable for appearing in films, with a 2003 V12 Vanquish appearing in the James Bond film Die Another Day.

ficha.descripcion: This casting is a depiction of the DeLorean time machine as it appears in Back to the Future Part III. When Doc and Marty want to leave 1885 they realize that the DeLorean cannot reach 88 miles per hour (142 km/h) under its own power since commercial gasoline is not yet available. Doc devises a plan to use a locomotive to push the DeLorean up to the required speed. Doc and Marty explore a rail spur they intend to use and spot an out-of-control horse-drawn wagon.

ficha.descripcion: This is a version of the Batmobile featured in Batman: The Animated Series; it is the second version of the Batmobile as featured in the series, with Batman using this version to replace an older Batmobile. The vehicle was designed by Earl Cooper, an automotive designer who was out of work; it was inspired by a similar vehicle Bruce Wayne had seen at the Gotham's World Fair. It is fitted with a turbine jet, grappling hook, ejection seats, onboard computer uplink and oil slick among other gadgets. Various copies of this design were later built to replace Batmobiles destroyed by Wayne's nemeses.

ficha.descripcion: The Citroën Type H, better known as the H Van, was a series of panel vans and light trucks produced by Citroën from 1947 to 1981. Designed by Flaminio Bertoni, these were intended to be simple, low-cost vans, using the same design philosophy as the 2CV. Most were sold in Europe and remain a common sight today as ice cream trucks or light commercial vehicles. 473,829 were produced. This casting depicts a Citroën H Van modified for racing, with both rear doors removed and what appears to be fire suppressant systems in the rear cargo hold.

ficha.descripcion: The H.I.S.S. Mk I GH7c (High Speed Sentry) is a tank used by Cobra, a terrorist organization and the main adversaries of the G.I. Joe Team. The H.I.S.S. was designed to fill anti-personnel and heavy armor roles and is highly maneuverable in various climates and environments. It is built with a modular design allowing mechanics to repair and replace broken parts with maximum efficiency; due to its design traits it is the most frequently used battle platform by Cobra. The turret can rotate.

ficha.descripcion: The Lotus Turbo Esprit is a two-seat sports car manufactured by Lotus Cars from 1981 to 1988. Designed by Giorgetto Giugiaro, the Turbo Esprit followed the previous Essex Turbo Esprit, a special edition of the Lotus Esprit S2 with a turbocharged engine and the first Lotus to come turbocharged from the factory. The Turbo Esprit was powered by a 2.2L 910 turbocharged inline-4 producing 210 horsepower mated to a 5-speed Citroën C35 manual; these could be differentiated from standard Esprits with their more aerodynamic and aggressive bodykit and unique "Turbo Esprit" logo marks. Production ended in 1988. 1,608 were produced. This is a replica of the 1980 Lotus Esprit Turbo Essex as seen in the James Bond film For Your Eyes Only. The base of the casting reads 1984 Lotus Esprit Turbo.

ficha.descripcion: This is a depiction of the fur-covered van in the film Dumb and Dumber, owned by Harry Dunne (portrayed by Jeff Daniels) and used for his Mutt Cutts dog grooming service. Nicknamed the Shaggin' Wagon, the vehicle is based on a 1984 Ford Econoline; a second version built from a Chevrolet Van was built for the film but never used. Both are covered in "more than 1,700 ft2" of 3-inch shag carpeting. Identified by the FBI in the film as an "'84 Sheepdog", the van is driven by Dunne, accompanied by his roommate and best friend Lloyd Christmas (portrayed by Jim Carrey); stranded in Nebraska with no money or gas, they sold the van to purchase a minibike instead in an attempt to get to Colorado. Christmas and Dunne would reunite with the van on the way to El Paso, Texas, as seen in Dumb and Dumber

Unlike the previous casting, this newer rendition is of all-metal construction and features rubbery plastic arms which can move independently; also unlike the previous casting the arms do not move as the car is rolled along, with no provisions for such a feature.

ficha.descripcion: The TMNT Party Wagon is a casting by Hot Wheels designed by Chris Colangelo, based on the original Party Wagon for the animated Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles series that ran from 1987 to 1996. The casting features moving parts such as a swing-out right door that features a blaster seat and turrets on the roof which can be moved up and down. The San Diego Comic-Con Exclusive release of the casting has extra pieces representing the four Ninja Turtles inside the interior, with Raphael and Leonardo on the front seat, Donatello on the back, and Michelangelo manning the blaster seat. These pieces were omitted from the Replica Entertainment release in 2020. A mainline version of the TMNT Party Wagon would later be released in 2020 as part of the HW Screen Time sub-segment, this time designed by Ma

ficha.descripcion: The Volkswagen Drag Truck is a pickup truck version of the Volkswagen Drag Bus. Unlike the Drag Bus, the Drag Truck is powered by two flat-4 engines and does not have a silhouette body conversion, with the combined bed cover and spoiler section being the moving piece. The casting was updated in 2005 with the base switching from triangle front wheel wells to rectangle wheel wells. The base of the casting reads Customized VW Drag Truck.

ficha.descripcion: The Ferrari Testarossa is a mid-engined sports car manufactured by Ferrari from 1984 to 1991. Styled by Emanuele Nicosa among others under Leonardo Fioravanti at Pininfarina, the Testarossa was the successor of Ferrari's older Berlinetta Boxer models and was first shown at the 1984 Paris Auto Show; the name Testarossa literally translates to "red head", paying homage to the earlier 250 Testa Rossa and its red-colored cam covers, which the Testarossa also features. The Testarossa was powered by a 4.9L F113 flat-12 mated to a 5-speed manual; this engine produced 385 horsepower. The Testarossa's styling is noted for its side strakes, nicknamed by the press as "cheese graters" but would later become a statement of style of the 1980s. The Testarossa was discontinued in 1991, replaced by the 512

ficha.descripcion: The '69 Dodge Daytona is a heavily modified and cartooned car of the same name. It was ironically introduced in 2003, the same year the real life car, introduced in 1996, was being retired. The tooling for this car was modified in 2016; the engine was slightly changed: it now has an open blower, open side windows and gained an actual sculpted interior. The First Edition has '70 Dodge Daytona on its base; this was later changed to '69 Dodge Daytona.

ficha.descripcion: The HKS TRB-01 is a highly-tuned 2000 Toyota Altezza modified by Japanese tuning company HKS for time attack racing. The car was intended to break records on the Tsukuba Circuit, hence its name of TRB-01 (Tsukuba Record Breaker). Few parts of the TRB-01 were shared with the road-going Altezza, with the car essentially being a custom build using vague Altezza bodylines on a tube frame chassis. It is powered by a 2.2L Toyota 3S-GE inline-4 with a HKS GT3037S turbo mated to a Xtrac 6-speed sequential; this was good for 600 horsepower. ficha.descripcion: The 'Tooned 69 Camaro Z28 is a cartoonish casting loosely based off of the actual production model. Like many 'Tooned vehicles, this one is noted for its short, chunky body, oversized engine and side exhausts. The tooling for the car was changed in 2016; the casting was retooled entirely. ficha.descripcion: Out-A-Line is a Blings-styled tuner car which highly resembles a Nissan Skyline GT-R R34, hence the name. Director Nathan Proch asked Sr. Designer Eric Tscherne to help make Out-A-Line a non licensed vehicle when Nissan did not approve it. Tscherne and Proch coined the name Out-A-Line since it was Not-A-Skyline. Despite this casting only having two releases, Out-A-Line was used for various Hot Wheels themed products including multiple bubble bath mixes, poppers, a birthday candle, and custom valve caps.

ficha.descripcion: The Wail Tale is a car featured in the Crooze series. It was in production for 2004 only and has never been used again. This car is based on the 1978 Porsche 935/78 racing car, nicknamed "Moby Dick". Keeping with Mattel's witty sense of humor for naming these models, it was named the Wail Tale. The name is a play-on-words of wail (yelling) to whale (a sea creature, Moby Dick; the nickname of the Porsche), and tale (story, legend) to tail (the rear portion of the car). And thus "translating" 'Moby Dick' to 'Wail Tail'.

ficha.descripcion: Even though it is named Lomad on the base, it is listed under the name 57 Nomad on the card for the 2005 First Editions series. This car is an obviously 'tooned' version of the classic wagon and #2 of 10 cars in the Drop Tops series. The Drop Tops were introduced in 2005 as flattened, cartoon-like versions of various vehicles. These cars are known to perform well on track sets as they benefit from their low center of gravity. Re-releases of Drop Tops vehicles have been somewhat limited.

ficha.descripcion: The Chevrolet Corvette (C2) (C2 for Second Generation), also known as the Corvette Sting Ray, is a sports car that was produced by Chevrolet for the 1963 to 1967 model years. This die-cast model is a 'tooned (from cartooned) version of the real life Sting Ray. It is a so-called Drop Top: a visual appearance that makes the roof lower than usual. The body sits low to the ground for a perfect center of gravity which gives the car more speed on the track. Re-releases have been relatively limited. The '63 Corvette Sting Ray is one of only two Drop Tops cars with a plastic base; the other is the Dodge Super 8 Hemi. To compensate the casting is very rear heavy.

ficha.descripcion: 2005 is the second year of what can be referred to as cartoonish casting designs. This design trend began in 2004. Blings are cartoonish-looking with wide, blingy rims. Drop Tops are flattened, with silhouettes well below the wheel wells. X-Raycers are made of striking, fruit candy-like, colorful see-through plastic. Torpedoes are deformed, elongated, open-wheel versions of real cars, like the '71 Charger, or Hot Wheels designs like the Overbored 454. ficha.descripcion: The Chrysler 300C (Blings) is a full-size luxury sedan produced by Chrysler, but designed in the Blings style with large wheels and short length compared to its height. The casting was retooled in 2015, with the lower bumper now being a separate piece of the body and the headlights and grille now being part of the windshield piece as opposed to being molded into the body. The base of the casting reads Chrysler 300.

Being a X-Raycer, this model has a plastic (often transparent) body and a metal base. The body sits low to the ground for a perfect center of gravity which gives the car more speed on the track. Due to the transparent plastic body some wonderful details can be seen: the massive V8 engine and even a miniature 360 Modena with a remote control in the front, under the trunk.

ficha.descripcion: The Mercedes-Benz G-Class, sometimes colloquially called the G-Wagen (as an abbreviation of Geländewagen) is a four-wheel drive automobile manufactured by Magna Steyr (formerly Steyr-Daimler-Puch) in Austria and sold by Mercedes-Benz. Originally developed as a military off-roader, later more luxurious models were added to the line. In certain markets, it has been sold under the Puch name as Puch G until 2000. The G-Wagon is characterised by its boxy styling and body-on-frame construction. It uses three fully locking differentials, one of the few passenger car vehicles to have such a feature. This casting depicts a Blings-styled version of the production car of the same name. According to the online Hot Wheels game Brakeless, it is implied that the wheels are over 26' inches.

ficha.descripcion: Speed Bump is a Drop Tops-styled personal luxury car of the 1940s and 1950s. The Drop Tops were introduced in 2005 as flattened, cartoon-like versions of various vehicles. These cars are known to perform well on track sets as they benefit from their low center of gravity. This casting has many features that make it a venerable choice in the die cast racing community It has proven to be one of the best track performing mainline cars in the modern Hot Wheels line up. Re-releases of Drop Tops vehicles have been somewhat limited.

ficha.descripcion: The Chevrolet Corvette is a sports car manufactured by the Chevrolet division of General Motors. The sixth generation, internally designated the C6 and designed by Tom Peters, was introduced in 2004 for the 2005 model year. This was the first Corvette generation since 1962 to have exposed headlights and featured revised suspension geometry, a 6.0L V8 and more refinement within the car. The convertible version of the Corvette, which this casting depicts, was introduced late in the 2005 model year. Production ended in 2013, to be replaced by the C7. This was the last 2009 New Model to be released. In comparison to the previous C6 Corvette casting from 2004 it features different proportioning and detailing. The casting was retooled in 2023, gaining a new interior in the process.

ficha.descripcion: Lamborghini offers some of the most exotic sports cars in the world, and with the latest Gallardo LP 560-4 coupe, that is no exception. This new "entry level" Lamborghini coupe was inspired by the Lamborghini Jalpa; a base model Lambo from the '80s, and delivers 560 horsepower at 8,000 rpm and 398 ft-lbs of torque at 6,500 rpm via a 5.2-liter V10 engine, making sure to deliver on the "Lamborghini experience" in full. The LP 560-4 was revealed at the 2008 Geneva Motor Show, as part of a mid-generation refresh. Later on the Lamborghini Gallardo LP 570-4 Superleggera was added to the lineup.

ficha.descripcion: The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution IX is the ninth generation of the Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution, the sports sedan and rally-tuned version of the Mitsubishi Lancer. ficha.descripcion: The GMC Typhoon is a high-performance SUV manufactured by GMC from 1992 to 1993. Designed by Kim Nielsen and Bill Davis, the Typhoon is in effect a SUV version of the Syclone introduced the previous year. As with the Syclone, the Typhoon is powered by a 4.3L Vortec LB4 turbocharged V6 mated to a 4-speed 4L60 automatic; unlike the Syclone, the Typhoon featured self-leveling rear suspension. The Typhoon was capable of accelerating from 0-60 mph (97 km/h) in 5.3 seconds and do the quarter mile in 14.1 seconds. The Typhoon was also available in a number of different color combinations, with different colors for the body and cladding. 4,391 were produced. This casting features an opening hood and model-year specific detailing.

ficha.descripcion:
The Haul of Flame is an adaption of a 2007 Ford E-450 Shuttle Bus, nicknamed the "Hot Wheels Shuttle". This was Larry Wood's last design as an employee of Hot Wheels before his retirement and move into what was effectively a consultant role and guest designer. From the backside of the 2009 Bonus Release: "The Red Line Club proudly presents the Haul of Flame.
This vehicle is an homage to the Mattel employee shuttle that operates daily at Mattel's headquartes in El Segundo, California, driving employees and guests between buildings. This Hot Wheels version of the employee shuttle has an exposed supercharged engine, zoomy pipes and a huge rear wing. If you know Hot Wheels, you will know the power of the flame!"

ficha.descripcion: The BMW 3.0 CSL Renncoupé is a racing variation of the BMW 3.0, internally known as the E9. The BMW 3.0 CSL was a Euro-spec 3.0 CS with aluminum bodywork to shed some weight for better on-track performance, with the CSL variant about 440 pounds (200 kg) less than the standard 3.0 CS. The 'L' standing for "leicht", German for 'Lightweight'. The Hot Wheels is based off the CSL that won in the European Touring Car Championship (ETCC) and in the from 1975 through until 1979 ETT+CC. 1,269 were produced. The base of the casting reads 75 BMW 3.0 CSL Race.

ficha.descripcion: The Ferrari 330 P4 is a mid-engined sport prototype racing car produced by Ferrari for endurance racing. Designed by Piere Drogo and Mauro Forghieri among others, the 330 P4 was an incremental upgrade of previous Ferrari P prototype models. Introduced in 1967, the 330 P4 was powered by a 4.0L Tipo 237 V12 mated to a 5-speed ZF manual; the engine was radically redesigned by Franco Rocchi with three-valve cylinder heads. Compared to the previous P model, the 330 P3, the 330 P4 was shorter and more powerful, generating 444 horsepower compared to the P3's 412. ficha.descripcion: The Toyota Hilux is a pickup truck manufactured by Toyota since 1968. Sold mostly as pickup trucks, the vehicle may be configured in a number of body styles. In recent years, the Hilux is notable for its extreme durability, being able to operate after sustained and heavy levels of abuse. The fifth generation Hilux was introduced in 1988 and featured a significant redesign over previous versions; it was also available in a long wheelbase variant. This was the last generation of the Hilux available in the United States, with Toyota opting to replace it with the Tacoma in 1995. This is a depiction of a stadium racing truck built in the style of a 1989 Toyota Hilux. The front wheels are slightly cambered. This was Charlie Angulo's first Elite 64 design.

ficha.descripcion: The Mercedes-AMG ONE is a very high-performance sports car manufactured by Mercedes-AMG from 2022 to 2025. Designed by Bálazs Filczer and Gorden Wagener, the AMG ONE acts as Mercedes-AMG's halo car and was initially unveiled as the Project ONE at the 2017 International Motor Show Germany. The AMG ONE is powered by a 1.6L PU106B Hybrid turbocharged V6 and hybrid system from the Mercedes F1 W06 Hybrid, with modifications done to allow the engine to comply with emissions regulations; this is mated to a 7-speed semi-automatic with a four-disc carbon racing clutch. The car features numerous applications of active aerodynamics, with an active rear wing and movable slats on the front fenders. Priced at $2.72 million, 275 units were produced; all have been sold out.

ficha.descripcion: The Freightliner Cascadia is a heavy-duty semi-trailer truck produced by Freightliner Trucks since 2007. The truck was designed with fuel efficiency in mind and improves upon other features used on other trucks in the Freightliner range. The Cascadia underwent a major design revision in 2018. This casting features a large die-cast trailer which can hold up to six models; it was started by Mark Jones but finished by Phil Riehlman. It is true to scale compared to other trucks done by Hot Wheels, it being the first truck to do so. This casting is based on the facelifted Cascadia with the AeroX Package with the lower clearance front bumper and roof deflectors. The casting is named the Cascadia Tractor with Trailer in the internal box sleeve.

ficha.descripcion: The McLaren M6GT is a sports prototype racing car designed and developed by McLaren to compete in endurance racing. Designed by Bruce McLaren, Robin Herd, Gordon Coppuck, Tyler Alexander and Don Beresford, the M6GT was based on the M6A but featured a closed cockpit. The car was powered by a 5.7L Chevrolet LT1 V8, similar to the M6A and other McLaren models of the time. Intended to be homologated for Group 4, homologation was never completed and as a result the M6GT never raced; two were later converted to road cars, one of which being Bruce McLaren's personal vehicle. 4 chassis were produced. The base of the casting reads McLaren M6 GT. This casting features an opening rear hatch.

ficha.descripcion: The Mercedes-Benz G 63 AMG 6×6 is a luxury sport utility truck manufactured by Mercedes-Benz from 2013 to 2015. A derivative of the G-Class, the G 63 AMG 6×6 combines the G 63 AMG's 5.5L M157 twin-turbocharged V8 with a large pickup truck-like body style, portal axles and a more luxurious interior. The vehicle was one of the most expensive Mercedes-Benz's produced at the time, priced at around $511,000, as well as one of the brand's most exclusive, with Mercedes-Benz declaring the car sold out in early 2015. Around 100 were produced.

ficha.descripcion: The Nissan 280ZX, internally known as the S130, is a sports car produced by Nissan from 1978 to 1983, sold under a number of different names depending on the market. It was the second generation of the Nissan Z car and was sold in 2-seat and 2+2-seat formats. This casting depicts a modified Nissan 280ZX with a Rocket Bunny Pandem kit. ficha.descripcion: The Porsche 928 is a luxury grand touring sports car produced by Porsche from 1978 to 1995. Designed by Wolfgang Möbius and Anatole Lapine, the 928 was Porsche's flagship model for a time. The original intention of the model was to replace the Porsche 911, which didn't exactly work as planned. 61,056 were produced. This casting depicts a modified Porsche 928 intended for off-roading, with a raised suspension, mudflaps, spotlights, and a roof rack. It is a significantly more detailed version of the mainline Porsche 928S Safari casting with different graphics and paintscheme and a slightly different appearance. This casting does not have any moving features.

ficha.descripcion: The Porsche 963 is a sport prototype racing car developed by Multimatic in collaboration with Porsche for endurance racing. Styled by Stéphane Lenglin under Grant Larson with design work by Christian Eifrig, the 963 is homologated for the LMDh category and competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship in the Hypercar class and the GTP class in the IMSA SportsCar Championship. It is powered by a 4.6L 9RD twin-turbocharged V8 mated to an Xtrac P1359 7-speed sequential; the engine is limited to 671 horsepower due to Balance of Performance regulations. A highly competitive car, the 963 won the 2024 IMSA SportsCar Championship with Porsche Penske Motorsport. The initial livery is based on chassis number LMD_003, the test car showcased at the 2022 Goodwood Festival of Speed.

ficha.descripcion: The 32 Ford Sedan is a Hot Wheels casting which debuted in the collector-aimed (100% Hot Wheels) Rod & Custom 2-Car Set. It is based on the real-life hot rod named Orange Crate owned by Bob Tindle in the 1960's. The real-life Orange Crate started life as a 1932 Ford Sedan (Tudor) which was already somewhat modified when bought by Bob in 1959. After appearing at the 1960 Portland Roadster Show, Bob decided to make an all-out show car. The Oldsmobile engine was enlarged to 417ci and a fully custom, chrome-plated tube chassis was built, and the body was modified to tilt up to reveal the excellent workmanship of the chassis. The Orange Crate was shown and won several awards at hot rod shows across the USA in 1961 to 1963 and also raced at the Winternationals where its best pass was 10.60 @

ficha.descripcion: The '34 Ford Lakes Coupe is a Hot Wheels casting which debuted in the collector-aimed (100% Hot Wheels) Bruce Meyer Gallery 4-Car Set. It is based on a record setting hot rod owned by the Pierson Brothers. It features a removable hood which reveals a detailed engine. It was used three times before being discontinued. The Pierson Brothers '34 Ford 3-window coupe is widely considered the most famous coupe in hot rod history. Brothers Dick and Bob built this record holding red to be run on dry lakes. It continuously set top speed records from the '50's through the '90's.

It is based on a real-life vehicle built by famed hot-rodder Boyd Coddington in the early 1990's powered by a Corvette LT1 engine. ficha.descripcion: The '48 Austin Coupe is a Hot Wheels casting which debuted in the collector-aimed (100% Hot Wheels) Classical Gassers 2-Car Set. It features a removable front section and was only released once before being discontinued. It is based on the car driven by 'Big John' Mazmanian in 1967. ficha.descripcion: From pamphlet in 4-car set: Barris Merc During the growing California custom scene of the '50s, the Barris brothers pioneered the chopped Mercury look. This favorite car of customizers got the typical Barris touch with chopped top and slanted B-pillars. It was nosed and decked and lowered. Filled with frenched headlights, Cadillac hubcaps, bubble skirts with teeth, and custom taillights. And finally finished off in the sweetest of Kandy Kolors. All trimmed out and ready to roll, any Barris Merc was a dare-to-be-different dream come true for America's car crazy youth!

ficha.descripcion: The 1953 Corvette was a legend in the making. America's first true sport car evolved from an artist's sketch pad to production in 18 short months. It was the first car to utilize a fiberglass body and all 300 hand-built beauties were quickly sold. Those first models, like european sportscars, had no exterior door handles or roll-up windows, but its trademark grill, with 13 sparkling chrome teeth, had consumers smiling for years to come. (From the Colectibles edition package) The '53 had a 235 cu in (3.9 L), 150HP in-line 6 engine, the Chevrolet's BlueFlame. Hot Wheels versions has opening hood and detailed engine.

ficha.descripcion: The Hirohata Merc is a custom 1951 Mercury Club Coupe built by Barris Customs. It was fabricated in 1953 by George and Sam Barris with Frank Sonzogni, for Bob Hirohata, a Japanese-American Navy Veteran and businessman. It has often been called "the most famous custom of the classic era" and had a "momentous effect" on car builders. The car was sold at a private auction in 2022, having changed hands a number of times prior. Hot Wheels replicated the Hirohata Merc in 1998 for the collector-aimed (100% Hot Wheels) in the Legends: Barris Kustom 4-Car Set. It was first produced to resemble the real-life mint green version, then for later releases, Hot Wheels created their own paint schemes. It was used 11 times before being discontinued. Its base and design are derived from the existing '49 Mer

ficha.descripcion: The 0032 Roadster is a Hot Wheels casting which debuted in the collector-aimed (100% Hot Wheels) America's Most Beautiful Roadster (AMBR) 2-Car Set. The real-life car was originally designed by Chip Foose in 1996 while working for Boyd Coddington where it won the AMBR award that year under the name 'Boydster II'. The car was eventually sold and in 2000 the new owner sought out Chip to redesign the car again. The updated version under the '0032' name won the 2000 AMBR award and currently resides in the Petersen Automotive Museum. The Hot Wheels version is based on the '0032' design of the car and was only used five times before being discontinued. The casting features an opening hood.

ficha.descripcion: During the period that Hot Wheels was releasing 100% Hot Wheels cars, they offered the basic Pro Racing series when NASCAR was at its height in popularity, which were essentially closed curbside models. Consequently, Hot Wheels created some lines of NASCAR Stockers in multiple scales that, just like the 100% Hot Wheels, were highly detailed with intricate pieces, featuring opening hoods to reveal engine detail. Not to be confused with the Pontiac Grand Prix Stocker (100%) which was released under the Hot Wheels Legends line and offers even more detail with removable body along with a clear display case (note that the shape of the casting differs slightly), and also the the Pontiac Grand Prix Stocker line which are basic curbside models.

ficha.descripcion: The Beatnik Bandit is a Hot Wheels casting which debuted in the 100% Hot Wheels Blood, Sweat & Gears 2-Car Set. It is based on the custom car created by Ed Roth in 1960. The real-life Beatnik Bandit was built on a shortened 1950 Oldsmobile chassis and featured an fiberglass custom body, complete with a bubble-top which doubled as both the roof and door. It also featured a unique "control stick" which operated the acceleration, brakes, steering and gear changes. The car still exists today and is on permanent display at the National Automobile Museum in Reno, Nevada. The Hot Wheels version debuted as part of the Original 16 from 1968 and was re-tooled in 1993 and 2012, although this version of the Beatnik Bandit differs from these. ficha.descripcion: Let's face it, the most eye-catching pickups on the road have been slammed and are cruisin' on glistening chrome wheels - BIG BODACIOUS WHEELS! Low-ridin' dubs have become wildly popular with everyone from sports and rap stars to to upscale urbanites. They have been an important part of custom car culture. Our Chevy crew cab truck fits the culture to a 'T' and offers a great deal on some big wheels ... in 1:64 scale. The Chevy Crew Cab is a Hot Wheels casting which debuted in the collector-aimed (100% Hot Wheels) Slammed Trucks 2-Car Set. It features an opening rear bed lid. It was used three times before being discontinued.

ficha.descripcion: Very shortly after the Hot Wheels Legends series was released, in 2000 Hot Wheels created a separate Crew's Choice series for their NASCAR lines in 1:64, 1:43 and 1:24 scale, while also in parallel having their other 100% castings appear in the late 90s and early 2000s. What makes the Crew's Choice series unique versus the later released similar Hot Wheels Racing Selects series, is that all of the models in this series have removable bodies, revealing a detailed engine and chassis. A total of 18 different models were known to have been produced. The Crew's Choice series was exclusively packaged in a small box decorated in the livery of the driver's car or in a black box for the larger scales, while the 1:64 Hot Wheels Racing Selects were sold in a clamshell package. ficha.descripcion: During the period that Hot Wheels was releasing the 100% Hot Wheels cars, they offered the basic Pro Racing series when NASCAR was at its height in popularity, which were essentially closed curbside models. Consequently, Hot Wheels created some lines of NASCAR Stockers in multiple scales that, just like the 100% Hot Wheels, were highly detailed with intricate pieces, featuring opening hoods to reveal engine detail. In this case they took the '01 Dodge Intrepid Stock Car and gave it the 100% Hot Wheels treatment. Only available in the 2001 Hot Wheels Racing Selects line. The '01 Dodge Intrepid Stock Car casting was used in the Showcase series, a series that usually has 100% Hot Wheels castings

ficha.descripcion:
Base name is Daytona 365 GTB, Package name Ferrari 365 GTS/4 "Daytona"
In 1968, Ferrari gambled with its new model, the "Daytona". With the competition turning to Mid-Engine designs, Ferrari introduced its flagship car with a front-engine layout. In keeping the cart behind the horse(power), Ferrari had produced a stunning coupe with an elongated hood, short rear deck and a comfortable, luxurious cabin. It was a instant hit and the 365 GTS/4 became one of Ferrari's most celebrated cars.

ficha.descripcion: Flamin' Frank's Fiat Coupe was a body shell over a fuel dragster chassis and engine. It smoked the quarter mile in 8.15 seconds at over 200 mph. But his car did something that had never been done, nor would ever be done again. His tires would actually light on fire during the run. Tragically, Frank died in a plane crash before he could share the secret to his popular pyrotechnic trick. The Fiat Coupe Dragster was a Hot Wheels casting which debuted in the 2004 Showcase Hot Wheels - Designer Series. It featured a removable body which displayed the interior of the dragster. It was only used twice before being discontinued.

ficha.descripcion: The Mysterion is a Hot Wheels casting which debuted in the 2001 Ed 'Big Daddy' Roth 4-Car Set in the 100% Hot Wheels Series. It is based on the real-life Mysterion which was a custom Hot Rod designed and built by Ed Roth in 1963. It featured two Ford engines and a bubble-top roof. After being featured on the front cover of Rod & Custom Magazine September 1963 and appearing at many car shows throughout the USA, the Mysterion changed hands several times and eventually was rediscovered in such poor condition that the car was dismantled and sold as parts.

In this case they took the Chevrolet Monte Carlo Stocker and gave it the 100% Hot Wheels treatment.

It was powered by an Oldsmobile 4.0L V8 which took the car from 0-60mp/h in 4.4 seconds. The Hot Wheels version featured an opening hood which displayed a detailed engine. It was only used twice before being discontinued.

ficha.descripcion: During the period Hot Wheels was releasing 100% Hot Wheels, the Pro Racing series was going as NASCAR was high in popularity. So Hot Wheels created a line of 1/64 NASCAR Stockers that, just like the 100% Hot Wheels, featured highly detailed intricate pieces, and hoods that opened up to show the engine. In this case they took the Ford T-Bird Stocker and gave it the 100% Hot Wheels treatment.

ficha.descripcion: During the period that Hot Wheels was releasing 100% Hot Wheels, they offered the basic Pro Racing series when NASCAR was at its height in popularity, which were essentially closed curbside models. Consequently, Hot Wheels created some lines of NASCAR Stockers in multiple scales that, just like the 100% Hot Wheels, were highly detailed with intricate pieces, featuring opening hoods to reveal engine detail. In this case they took the 2000 and 2001 Taurus Stocker and gave it the 100% Hot Wheels treatment.

ficha.descripcion: Tommy Ivo is one of the greatest showmen in drag racing history. Nicknamed 'TV Tommy' & 'Instant Ivo' from his career as an actor in nearly 200 TV shows and films, his star burned brightest on the drag strip. Tommy was the first driver to run in the 8s on gas and in the 7s on fuel. He was the first inductee into the Cragar 5-Second Club, the International Drag Racing Hall of Fame, and garnered a life-time achievement award from the NHRA. Tommy Ivo's AA/F Dragster is a Hot Wheels casting which debuted in the collector-aimed (100% Hot Wheels) Showcase Hot Wheels - Racing Series. It was only used twice before being discontinued.

According to designer Charlie Angulo, the Character Car's original body was initially considered for use, but didn't seem to fit as well on the Monster Truck chassis and "didn't look as cool"; an entirely new body would be used instead as Mattel had the opportunity to create an all new tool.
